columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 600M+ monthly active users globally; roughly 236M–250M paid subscribers (late 2024–2025).
2023 revenue ≈€13–15B, premium subscriptions ~87% of revenue, ads ~13%.
Formats: music, podcasts, audiobooks, plus AI DJs, short-form music videos, and interactive content.

strengths.title: Best-in-class personalization and discovery
strengths.detail: Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Daily Mixes, Blend, AI DJ, Smart Shuffle, and Enhance (adds up to 30 recommended songs per playlist, toggleable).

strengths.title: Huge catalog and multi-format support
strengths.detail: Tens of millions of tracks plus podcasts, audiobooks, and exclusive shows, strong breadth across formats.

strengths.title: Cross-platform UX
strengths.detail: Native apps for mobile, desktop, web, smart TVs, consoles, cars, and smart speakers with a consistent experience.

strengths.title: Social and collaborative features
strengths.detail: Collaborative playlists, Blend shared mixes, following friends/artists, and listening stats, a strong social layer around music.

weaknesses.title: Audio quality vs HD competitors
weaknesses.detail: Standard streams often rated lower than Apple Music or Amazon Music HD/Ultra HD, which include Hi-Res at similar prices.

weaknesses.title: Algorithm reliance and filter bubbles
weaknesses.detail: Heavy recommendation reliance can create filter bubbles; some users feel the algorithm over-pushes popular tracks or moods.

weaknesses.title: Podcasts and audiobooks integration trade-offs
weaknesses.detail: Multi-format main app can clutter the UI; navigation feels more complex than dedicated audio apps for some users.

weaknesses.title: Free tier limitations
weaknesses.detail: Ads, limited skips, and shuffle-only playback for some users; offline and full on-demand require Premium.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Spotify is music and podcast listening at massive scale, playlists, shows, and daily listen habits. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Spotify is a global audio streaming service that gives you access to millions of songs and podcasts, with personalized playlists and recommendations.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Spotify side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Spotify you can use Audio and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with Spotify

You can use both. Spotify keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on Spotify, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
